metadata.name: APEX-008-25
metadata.description: An OAuth implementation with vulnerable redirect_uri validation allowing authorization code theft

matched.actualTitle: OAuth Redirect URI Validation Bypass via startsWith Prefix Check
matched.matchReason: Both describe the same vulnerability: weak redirect_uri validation using startsWith() method instead of proper URI parsing. The actual finding demonstrates the exact attack vectors mentioned in the expected finding (subdomain tricks via app.vulnerable.local.attacker.com, port modification, and path manipulation). The CRITICAL severity of the actual finding is justified given the authorization code exfiltration impact.

matched.actualTitle: OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI Validation Bypass via Incomplete Prefix Check
matched.matchReason: This is an alternate representation of the same vulnerability from a different testing perspective. It covers the same prefix check weakness with additional bypass vectors (domain extension, URL authority bypass with @ symbol, query parameter injection, and fragment manipulation). All represent the same underlying weakness in redirect_uri validation.

matched.actualTitle: OAuth Redirect URI Validation Bypass (Open Redirect) - Authorization Code Exfiltration
matched.matchReason: Third variant of the same vulnerability, demonstrating the actual exploitation scenario with an authenticated user (admin bot) approving an authorization request with a malicious redirect_uri. Shows the complete attack chain from weak validation to code exfiltration to the attacker's domain (app.vulnerable.local.attacker.com/steal).

extra.title: Framework Fingerprinting via X-Powered-By Header and HTTP Method Enumeration
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The health endpoint exposes Express.js framework information and enumerates all available HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, PUT, PATCH, POST, DELETE), enabling attackers to conduct targeted reconnaissance specific to Express.js vulnerabilities.

extra.title: No Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint - Enables Credential Stuffing and Brute Force Attacks
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The login endpoint lacks any rate limiting, account lockout, or brute force protection mechanisms. Testing confirmed 50+ rapid sequential login attempts were all accepted immediately, enabling credential stuffing and dictionary attacks.

extra.title: CORS Misconfiguration Enables CSRF Attacks in OAuth Flow
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - OAuth endpoints implement dangerous CORS configuration with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true combined with reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin, violating OAuth 2.0 security best practices and enabling CSRF attacks against OAuth flows.

extra.title: Service Type Information Disclosure via Health Endpoint
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The health endpoint explicitly discloses the service type as 'oauth-provider' in JSON response, enabling attackers to identify the application purpose and conduct targeted reconnaissance of OAuth-specific attack vectors.

extra.title: Bearer Token Scheme Case Sensitivity Vulnerability
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The userinfo endpoint's Bearer token validation is case-sensitive, rejecting lowercase 'bearer' schemes and returning different error messages. This violates RFC 6750 which requires case-insensitive authorization scheme matching.

extra.title: OAuth State Fixation Vulnerability - Predictable State Parameter
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The OAuth state parameter is deterministically generated from only the return pathname with no randomization. State value 'eyJyZXR1cm5QYXRobmFtZSI6Ii8ifQ%3D%3D' is identical across multiple requests, allowing attackers to predict state values and potentially enable CSRF attacks.

extra.title: Registered OAuth Client Applications Enumeration
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The root endpoint directly exposes registered client applications ('vulnerable-app'), and the authorization endpoint provides differential error responses that enable enumeration of valid vs invalid client_ids.

extra.title: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Misconfiguration - Arbitrary Origin Allowed with Credentials
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The health endpoint reflects arbitrary Origin headers in CORS responses while allowing credentials (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true), allowing any website to access the endpoint on behalf of authenticated users.

extra.title: Hardcoded Credentials Exposed in Login Page HTML
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The login page contains hardcoded demo credentials in HTML comments: 'user/user123' and 'admin/SuperSecretAdminPass123!'. The admin account with hardcoded password is particularly critical for privilege escalation.

extra.title: Implicit Grant Type (Token Response Type) Supported and Advertised
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The OAuth server supports the implicit grant type (response_type=token) which is inherently less secure than authorization code flow due to token exposure in browser history, Referer headers, and inability to use refresh tokens.

extra.title: Logout Functionality Vulnerable to CSRF Attacks - GET Request Not Protected
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The logout endpoint accepts GET requests without CSRF protection and doesn't properly invalidate sessions. Sessions remain valid after logout, and attackers can force logout via simple image tags or redirects.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Health/Status Endpoint Exposed
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The health check endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication, allowing attackers to determine server availability and status, and revealing service type information.

extra.title: Exposed API Documentation at Root Endpoint
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - The root endpoint exposes complete API documentation including all available endpoints (/oauth/authorize, /oauth/token, /oauth/userinfo, /login) and registered client applications without requiring authentication.
